problems.summary: The same wall bound fired again, in the complementary mode: last iteration it killed a turn whose work was already durable and lost only the report, whereas here it killed a turn that had written nothing, because Arch assigned a one-pass rewrite of a 781-line document so all output was scheduled for a single terminal Write. Zero artifacts survived.
problems.evidence: Event 1eeea99a2d7c415fa1fcd78def37b01f: duration_seconds 1800.044, returncode 143, error timeout, 13 tool calls, 452,399 cache-read tokens. git status clean and both target files byte-identical to HEAD after the turn. The turn's own report states the shape directly: 'now drafting the complete replacement document in one pass'. Second occurrence of this category in two consecutive retrospectives.

problems.summary: Arch let --budget-kind default to the workflow kind, allocating the documentation class's 30 minutes to a ~1,040-line prose rewrite, and separately believed --timeout 2700 would reserve partial-handoff headroom beyond a 30-minute budget. Both were wrong, and together they left the issue scope exhausted and unable to accept another dispatch.
problems.evidence: Scope issue:1DMIX-052 after one turn: wall 30/30 EXHAUSTED while calls stood at 13/120 and spend at $5/$15 -- wall clock was the only exhausted dimension. team_budget.reserve computes deadline as min(deadlines) across the issue scope and the requested turn, so the turn died at 1800.04 s rather than the requested 2700 s, and its receipt's deadline/soft_deadline gap of 360 s is the scope's value, not the turn's. team_budget.DEFAULTS shows documentation at 30 minutes, tied with scientific_small for the smallest time allocation of any class.

solutions.reason: Already open and owns exactly this mechanism; this iteration adds the complementary failure mode (nothing durable) to the mode it was filed for (durable work, lost report), which strengthens rather than changes its case.

Filed this iteration with the measured scope figures. The corrective discipline is Arch-side and lands immediately in the next preparation; the record exists so the discipline is auditable rather than remembered.

carry_forward: Shape any long-output assignment so each completed unit is written to disk before the next begins; a single terminal Write turns any bound into total loss.
An issue scope's effective turn deadline is the minimum of the scope's remaining wall time and the requested --timeout, so --timeout cannot buy time the scope does not have.
Treat a timed-out dispatch as work-of-unknown-completeness: inspect the tree before re-dispatching, and resume with followup rather than restarting.
